newsitem.title: INDIA: India reshuffles panel to combat economic crimes.
newsitem.headline: India reshuffles panel to combat economic crimes.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P.Chidambaram will head an Economic Intelligence Council (EIC), which is being reconstituted to evolve an effective strategy to combat economic crimes, the government said on Wednesday.

The council would discuss measures to coordinate the work of law enforcement agencies, monitor important cases involving coordination, and keep a watch on economic crimes to suggest effective measures to deal with them, it said in a statement.

The panel would discuss measures to strengthen law enforcement, advise on legal changes and plugging of legal loopholes to in order to take action against economic offenders, and act as a forum for exchange of intelligence on important economic offences, the statement said.
The council would also discuss measures to combat the generation and laundering of black money and formulate strategies against black money and tax evasion, it said.

Senior officials including the Finance Secretary, Revenue Secretary, the governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the chairman of the regulatory Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) would be among its members, it said.

The director-general of the Narcotics Control Bureau and the Company Affairs Secretary are among other officials who would be in the 18-member council, which would include the chiefs of the Central Board of Direct Taxes and the Central Board of Excise and Customs.
